Issued at 324 PM CST Thu Nov 19 2026

Currently through tonight...

Was a bit of a dreary start to the day for south-southwestern  
locations...as a swath of fog and low cloud cover stretched
across the forecast area. Had a handful of counties impacted 
by dense fog...satellite imagery showing that having largely 
diminished by around midday. Through the rest of the 
afternoon...expecting more sun, but increasing upper level 
clouds will be streaming in from west to east. Upper level data 
showing shortwave ridging working its way across the Plains 
today, keeping things dry...set up between one area of low 
pressure in the Great Lakes region, with a larger system along 
the West Coast. At the surface, the overall pattern is on the 
weaker side...the day started with more light/variable winds, 
with time winds have become more south-southeasterly as sfc low 
pressure deepens a bit over the High Plains. Speeds through the 
rest of the afternoon look to generally top out around 10-15 
MPH, though an occasional gust closer to 20 isn't out of the 
question. High temperatures looking to top out in the mid-60s 
for most locations.

Dry conditions continue on this evening/overnight...expecting  
increasing southerly winds with time as the sfc pressure
gradient tightens across the region thanks to further 
deepening of that sfc low over the High Plains. Gusts closer to 
25-30 MPH will be possible. 

Friday through the weekend...

Look to the end of this week into the upcoming weekend...overall 
there hasn't been any significant changes to the forecast. The 
best chances for precipitation remain focused in the late day 
Saturday-Saturday evening time frame. 

During the day on Friday, models remain in good agreement in the
big picture...the upper level pattern remaining southwesterly 
as that system currently over the West Coast pushes further 
inland. By the end of the day...models showing the strongest, 
main upper low moving through western Canada, with 
troughing/embedded shortwaves extending south through the 
Rockies into western portions of the Desert SW. At the surface, 
our forecast area remains west of the main trough axis/frontal 
boundary, which looks to be draped from the central Dakotas into
the NE/KS/CO border area by the end of the day. The tighter 
pressure gradient is expected to make for a windy day...with 
southerly sustained speeds around 25-30 MPH and gusts in the 
35-45 MPH possible. Forecast highs aren't notably different than
today, some spots will be warmer...overall topping out in the 
mid- upper 60s.

Friday evening-overnight...the surface cold front will working
its way further into the forecast area, which could bring some
isolated/scattered precipitation. Models differ on whether 
there is any activity or it remains dry...kept some low-end 
precip chances in the NW through the evening, with sprinkles 
through the rest of the overnight hours. Recent runs of the 
HRRR/RRFS have kept things dry overnight. 

For Saturday, where this sfc front ultimately ends up is one of
the biggest questions for the day...as that will drive where 
better precipitation chances develop. Models the past few days 
have gone back and forth some with how much progress the front 
makes as the main upper low pushes further east along the ND/Can
border and shortwave energy is moving roughly along the KS/OK 
border. Models like the EC/GEM remain on the broader/slower 
side, keeping chances further west and over much more of the 
forecast area...others like the GFS/RRFS keeping it more 
confined to our SErn locations, roughly east of a York County to
Rooks County line. Precipitation chances in the forecast (at 
least the low end/20 percent line) remains broad at this point 
Saturday afternoon, including all by the extreme western fringe 
of the forecast area. Models continue to show things being a 
liquid event. The daytime passage of the cold front and 
increasing precip chances continues to make for a tricky, lower- 
confidence forecast...highs range from the low 40s in the NW to 
around 60 in the SE.

Things dry back out for Sunday, with more zonal, progressive
upper level flow setting up across the region and no notable 
disturbances moving through. Expecting fairly light winds around
10 MPH...with highs topping out in the low-mid 40s.

New work week/Thanksgiving Day...

Forecast remains dry for the start of the new work week...with
focus turning to the next upper level disturbance. This system
will be working its way through the Rockies during the day on 
Monday, but there are some slight timing differences between 
models. Will likely see increasing cloud cover from west to east
with time, but winds looking to remain on the lighter side of 
things around 10-15 MPH. Not much change for temps, with highs 
still in the low-mid 40s for most. 

This disturbance makes its way onto the Plains Monday night into 
Tuesday...but along with the slight timing differences, there is
also some differences with the track. T
